query: What were the main causes of the 2008 global financial crisis?
report:
## Origins of the Crisis

Subprime mortgage lending was a central cause of the crisis [1]. Securitisation packaged those mortgages into mortgage-backed securities and collateralised debt obligations, which spread the risk across the financial system [2]. Excessive leverage at financial institutions amplified the resulting losses [3].

## The Lehman Failure

Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008 with 691 billion dollars in assets [4].

## References

[1] Federal Reserve History. Subprime mortgage crisis. Retrieved from https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/subprime-mortgage-crisis
[2] Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission. Securitisation and derivatives. Retrieved from https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GPO-FCIC/pdf/GPO-FCIC.pdf
[3] Bank for International Settlements. Leverage and the crisis. Retrieved from https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt0803.htm
[4] Lehman Brothers bankruptcy filing. Retrieved from https://www.sec.gov/edgar/lehman

sources.title: Subprime mortgage crisis
sources.content: Subprime mortgage lending was a central cause of the crisis. Lenders originated mortgages to borrowers with weak credit, and those loans were then pooled and sold.

sources.title: Securitisation and derivatives
sources.content: Securitisation packaged subprime mortgages into mortgage-backed securities and collateralised debt obligations. This spread the risk across the financial system and obscured where it sat.

sources.title: Leverage and the crisis
sources.content: Excessive leverage at financial institutions amplified the losses once asset prices fell. Highly leveraged balance sheets forced rapid deleveraging.

sources.title: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy filing
sources.content: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008, listing 639 billion dollars in assets, the largest bankruptcy filing in United States history.
